shift.rhythm: The day starts with setting up the surgery, gets busier through treatments and turnarounds, includes handling unexpected changes, and finishes by closing down.

people.name: Priya Nair
people.note: Supervises you, explains routines, and supports your learning.

people.name: Dr Hannah Reid
people.note: The clinician you are assisting today in Surgery 2.

frame.morningBrief: Morning. I’m Priya, senior dental nurse here — I’m your mentor, so today you’re with me, 08:15 to half five. Here’s the list. Six patients this morning for Dr Reid, four this afternoon. First in is Amira — ten years old, first filling, coming with her dad. Before anyone sits in that chair the surgery has to be clean, working and stocked, the emergency kit checked, and a tray ready for her. Then we look after Amira, then we reset, then we go again. You don’t need to know any of the kit yet — I’ll show you as we go, and if you’re not sure about anything, ask. That’s not a weakness in this job. It’s the job.
frame.closeOfDay: Half five. Good shift. You checked the safety critical stuff, you listened to the patients, and you adapted when the morning went sideways. It’s not just passing instruments, is it? We’re managing the people, the infection control, and the clinician’s time all at once. Some days it is exhausting, but it’s real healthcare. Have a think tonight if this is what you want to do. If it is, you’ve got the right attitude for it. I’ll sign off your day.
frame.tone: Clear, warm, professional. The mentor is calm, practical and encouraging, using short sentences.

tasks.title: Set up the surgery for the morning
tasks.situation: The practice has just opened. Surgery 2 is cold and quiet, the check sheets are blank, and the first patient, Amira, is due at 09:00 for a composite filling.
tasks.job: Get yourself ready, flush the water lines for the right time, check the emergency kit and set up the tray for the 09:00 filling, checking every pouch.

materials.name: Surgery check sheet
materials.description: The daily start-of-day checks: water lines, suction, autoclave, surfaces, stock. Signed with date, time and initials.

materials.name: Medical emergency equipment check sheet
materials.description: The emergency drugs box and oxygen: present, in date, sealed. Anything out of date is flagged and reported.

materials.name: Tray set-up guide: composite filling
materials.description: The instruments and materials for the 09:00, with a pouch check on every item.

tasks.interaction: Priya shows you each routine once and then watches you do it.
tasks.doneWhen: The preparation steps are in order, the check sheet shows a 2-minute flush, the expired glucagon is reported, and the tray matches the guide with the broken-seal pouch set aside.
tasks.whatHappensNext: You prepare to welcome the first patient.
tasks.complication: Opening the emergency drugs box: one of the drugs, the glucagon, is past its expiry date.

tasks.title: Welcome Amira and her dad
tasks.situation: Amira (10) is in the waiting room with her dad, Karim. Her notes flag: nervous, first filling, dad attending, mild asthma with a blue inhaler. Karim says she didn't sleep much.
tasks.job: Collect them by name, settle Amira in the chair, record what dad tells you, and answer their questions within your role.

materials.name: Amira's notes
materials.description: Nervous, first filling, dad attending, mild asthma with a blue inhaler.

materials.name: Settling-in routine
materials.description: Coats, seat, warn before the chair moves, bib, glasses. Amira chooses the colour.

tasks.interaction: You speak to Amira and Karim directly. Priya is behind you and Dr Reid is in the surgery.
tasks.doneWhen: The greeting names Amira and includes dad with no pain promise, Amira is settled with dad in view, the antibiotics and inhaler are recorded and flagged to Dr Reid, and both questions are answered within an apprentice's role.
tasks.complication: As the light comes on over the chair, Amira's eyes fill and she grips the armrests. Dad looks at you.

tasks.title: Support the filling
tasks.situation: Dr Reid has explained the filling and agreed the hand-up signal with Amira. Dad is on the stool by the door. The tray you set up is beside you.
tasks.job: Work the suction, have the next item ready before Dr Reid asks, pass instruments safely and watch Amira's face more than you watch the tooth.

materials.name: Procedure strip
materials.description: Numb, keep dry, remove decay, etch, bond, composite in layers with the band on first, cure, check the bite and polish.

materials.name: Tray
materials.description: The instruments and materials you set up this morning, including the curing light and its barrier sleeve.

tasks.interaction: You assist Dr Reid chairside. Priya watches from the door.
tasks.doneWhen: The needle is left to Dr Reid, the suction is placed well, all four next-item prompts are answered, instruments pass below the chin, the hand signal is reported instantly and handled, and the curing light goes out sleeved with the shield.
tasks.complication: Water collects at the back of Amira's mouth while the handpiece runs, and her hand lifts from the armrest.

tasks.title: The job isn't finished: notes, aftercare and reset
tasks.situation: The filling is done. Amira is still numb, Dr Reid needs the notes finishing with batch numbers, dad needs the aftercare, and the 09:40 check-up has arrived.
tasks.job: Look after Amira as the treatment ends, record the notes and batch numbers, give dad the approved aftercare, hand Sam the recall note, then reset Surgery 2 in order.

materials.name: Patient notes and packaging
materials.description: Fields for treatment, anaesthetic and material batch numbers, aftercare and recall. Batch is the lot number, not the product code or expiry.

materials.name: Aftercare card: fillings (children)
materials.description: The three approved points to give a parent.

materials.name: Reset-between-patients routine
materials.description: Ten steps from PPE on to the new tray and check sheet, with a 20 to 30 second flush.

tasks.interaction: You speak to Amira and Karim, hand over to Sam at reception, and reset the room while Priya watches the door.
tasks.doneWhen: Amira's end-of-treatment care is in order, the notes carry the batch numbers and a six-month recall, the three approved aftercare points are given, the recall note is with reception, and Surgery 2 is reset in order with no step skipped.
tasks.whatHappensNext: You move to the decontamination room.
tasks.complication: A message from Sam: "09:40 has been waiting 10 mins. How long?" The clock is slipping.

tasks.title: The morning changes
tasks.situation: You are at the inspection lamp with Amira's instruments. Priya has been called next door. Then Joanne arrives: the 10:20 has cancelled, Mr Nowak is coming at 10:40 in severe pain, and a delivery is blocking the corridor.
tasks.job: Finish the decontamination step you are on safely, then decide what to do first, what can wait and who needs to know, and get Surgery 2 ready for 10:40.

materials.name: Decontamination cycle card
materials.description: Scrub below 45°C, rinse, inspect, autoclave spaced with indicators, cool covered, pouch dry within an hour, label with expiry and initials, store. Log every cycle.

materials.name: Examination tray guide
materials.description: Mirror, probe, tweezers, cotton rolls, ejector and aspirator tips, 3-in-1 tip, bib, glasses. Dr Reid asked for the emergency drugs box within reach.

materials.name: Updated day list and delivery note
materials.description: 10:20 struck through. 10:40 Mr N, emergency, pain, exam, Dr Reid. A delivery including local anaesthetic and disinfectant concentrate.

tasks.interaction: Joanne, the practice manager, asks what you are doing first. Priya is next door and answers by message.
tasks.doneWhen: The inspected instruments are sorted, the autoclave is started and logged, the four jobs are ranked with one request for help, Priya has a short message with no clinical guess, Surgery 2 is ready with the exam tray and drugs box, the delivery is out of the corridor with the special-storage items flagged, and the load is pouched within the hour.
tasks.complication: Joanne: "Three things. 10:20's cancelled. Mr Nowak's coming at 10:40 in a lot of pain. And there's a delivery in the corridor that Sam's about to fall over."

tasks.title: Graham's first visit in ten years, and closing the day
tasks.situation: Graham Ellis (54) is a new patient: extremely anxious, no dentist in over ten years, asked for a nurse to collect him and wants to talk first. Priya says this one is yours.
tasks.job: Bring Graham in so he stays in control, support him through the examination without judging him, record what Dr Reid dictates, then close the surgery and write your handover.

materials.name: Graham's patient card
materials.description: New patient exam. Nurse to collect, wants to talk first, bad experience as a teenager. High blood pressure, medicated; no allergies.

materials.name: The examination in plain words
materials.description: A small mirror and a thin instrument, counting and noting. Any X-rays only with his agreement.

materials.name: End-of-session close-down card and handover template
materials.description: Disinfectant through the aspirator at the end of the session. Handover: what is ready, what is outstanding, what to watch.

tasks.interaction: You lead with Graham. Dr Reid examines and dictates; Priya is in the room but lets you run it.
tasks.doneWhen: Graham is approached beside him with a line that gives him control, offered control and information, answered without judgement, given his minute, his distress is reported to Dr Reid, the factual note and booking slip are done, and the close-down and handover are complete.
tasks.complication: As Dr Reid reaches for the mirror, Graham sits up: "Sorry. I need a minute outside." He stands.
